cards: Madeleine Colani publishes her nine excavations in the northern Vietnamese province of Hòa Bình
The First Congress of Prehistorians of the Far East defines the Hoabinhian
J. M. Matthews shows that the cobble tools of Sai Yok form a continuous range rather than Colani’s distinct types
A conference in Hanoi votes to keep the term and to call the Hoabinhian an industry of the late Pleistocene to mid Holocene
Hoabinhian artefacts dating from 41,500 BCE are recognised at the Xiaodong rock shelter in Yunnan, 40 km from the border with Myanmar
The French Archaeological Mission in the Indus Basin, led by Jean-François and Catherine Jarrige, discovers the site
A study in the journal Nature reports drilled human teeth from the Neolithic graveyard
John Marshall announces the discovery of a forgotten civilisation of the Indus
Steve Young finds pottery in a village path, and samples are later sent to the University of Pennsylvania for dating
Ban Chiang becomes a UNESCO World Heritage Site
US federal raids ending Operation Antiquity uncover thousands of looted Ban Chiang artefacts in California museums
Swami Vivekananda introduces Hinduism to the World’s Parliament of Religions in Chicago
The constitution of the Republic of India abolishes untouchability
Aryabhata writes his treatise on astronomy and mathematics in Sanskrit verse
William Jones points out the common origin of Sanskrit, Greek and Latin
India’s constitution lists Sanskrit among the languages of the nation
Plain Grey Ware is found at Anuradhapura in Sri Lanka in levels of 600–500 BCE, showing connections with northern India
Excavations at Alamgirpur, near Delhi, reveal an overlap between late Harappan and the earliest Painted Grey Ware levels
Two periods of Painted Grey Ware are identified at Ahichhatra, c. 1500–800 and 800–400 BCE
1,576 Painted Grey Ware sites are known
The mound at Adichanallur is first dug, and its finds go to the Berlin ethnological museum
Mortimer Wheeler excavates Brahmagiri, helping to establish the culture sequence of south Indian prehistory
The Austrian archaeologist Franz Heger, creator of a classification of bronze drums, turns to the drums
A fisherman, Nguyễn Văn Lắm, reports bronze finds to the École française d’Extrême-Orient, and excavations begin at Đông Sơn village
B. R. Ambedkar and hundreds of thousands of his followers become Buddhists at Nagpur
The Pali Text Society is founded to publish romanised Pali texts and English translations
The Government of India designates Pali a classical language of India
Elara, a Chola general or prince, takes the throne of Anuradhapura and rules for forty-four years
U. V. Swaminatha Aiyar finds major Sangam manuscripts at the Thiruvavaduthurai Adhinam
Portuguese missionaries print the prayer book Thambiran Vanakkam, making Tamil the first Indian language to be printed and published
Tamil becomes the first legally recognised classical language of India
Halin's wooden city gates, its earliest dated artefacts, are made; the city in the Mu valley grows into the largest Pyu centre.
The Pyu adopt the Sakra Era, two years after it came into use in India.
On 22 March the Vikrama dynasty at Sri Ksetra launches a new calendar, which later becomes the Burmese calendar.
On 25 March King Duttabaung founds Sri Ksetra's second dynasty.
Sri Ksetra's embassy, with 35 musicians singing in Sanskrit, reaches the Tang court.
Nanzhao warriors overrun the Pyu country and take 3,000 prisoners from Halin.
Fan Chan sends embassies to India and China; around 245 the Chinese describe walled villages, palaces, archives and taxes paid in gold, silver, pearls and perfumes.
Jayavarman, 'Protégé of Victory', begins a reign that lasts until his death in 514.
Rudravarman kills his brother Gunavarman for the throne and becomes the last known king of Funan, reigning to about 545.
Khu Liên, an official at Xianglin, rebels against the Eastern Han dynasty and founds Lâm Ấp, the predecessor state of Champa.
The Sui Empire invades Lâm Ấp, overruns Sambhuvarman's resistance and sacks the capital at Trà Kiệu.
Indravarman II founds Indrapura and a Buddhist dynasty; the years to 982 are called the Golden Age of Champa art.
Jaya Indravarman IV's fleet takes Angkor by surprise, kills the Khmer king and begins a four-year Cham occupation of Cambodia.
Lê Thánh Tông's army destroys Vijaya; 120,000 Cham are killed or captured and the kingdom shrinks to Kauthara and Panduranga.
Minh Mạng arrests the last king, Po Phaok The, and annexes Panduranga as the provinces of Ninh Thuận and Bình Thuận.
Narasimhavarman I sacks Vatapi; the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II dies
Pulakeshin I fortifies the hill of Vatapi and performs a horse sacrifice
Ravikirti composes the Aihole inscription celebrating Pulakeshin II
Pallava king Narasimhavarman I takes Vatapi; Pulakeshin II dies
On 13 April Narasimhagupta, vassal of Bhavavarman I, erects a figure of Vishnu at Isanapura; the same year Bhavavarman builds a temple at the centre of his kingdom of Bhavapura.
On 14 June Jayavarman I, son of Candravarman, issues his earliest inscriptions; his reign of about thirty years is the last over a united Chenla.
After the end of the Shenlong era the Tang histories record Chenla divided into Land Chenla (Wendan) and Water Chenla.
On 5 April Queen Jayadevi, ruling at Angkor, complains of 'bad times' in her Western Baray inscription as the kingdom breaks into principalities.
Jayavarman II proclaims the Khmer Empire, ending the pre-Angkor period.
Dnyaneshwar completes the Dnyaneshwari, a Marathi verse commentary on the Bhagavad Gita
Chaitanya Mahaprabhu becomes a renunciant and settles at Puri, spreading the chanting of Krishna’s names
Tulsidas begins the Ramcharitmanas, the story of Rama retold in the Awadhi form of Hindi
The Chinese pilgrim Yijing visits Srivijaya on his way to India
The Kedukan Bukit inscription records Sri Jayanasa's military expedition
The Medang court in Java is destroyed by the rebellion of the ruler of Wurawari
Rajendra Chola I sacks Srivijaya and its ports and captures its ruler
Kertanagara of Singhasari launches the Pamalayu expedition against Malayu
Traditional date for Tarusbawa’s founding of the kingdom of Sunda
Sanghyang Tapak inscriptions of King Sri Jayabupati
King Linggabuana is killed by Majapahit troops in the Battle of Bubat
Sunda signs a treaty of alliance with the Portuguese of Malacca
Fatahillah’s forces capture Sunda Kalapa, later Jakarta
Surawisesa sets up the Batutulis inscription honouring his father
Maulana Yusuf of Banten takes and destroys Pakuan Pajajaran
The Kedukan Bukit inscription near Palembang, the earliest known stone inscription in Old Malay, is written in the Pallava script
The Portuguese capture Malacca; the court moves to Johor and Malay literary centres scatter across the archipelago
The Anglo-Dutch Treaty divides the Malay world between Dutch and British rule, both of which use Malay to centralise and modernise
Indonesia’s constitution makes Indonesian, developed from Riau Malay, the national language
Malay becomes the sole official language of Peninsular Malaysia
Alauddin Khalji captures Chittor after an eight-month siege
Rana Sanga is defeated by Babur at the Battle of Khanwa
Udai Singh II founds Udaipur on Lake Pichola
Akbar takes Chittor after a siege of several months
Maharana Pratap fights a Mughal army at the Battle of Haldighati
Amar Singh I accepts Mughal overlordship on honourable terms
Udaipur joins the United State of Rajasthan; Bhupal Singh becomes Rajpramukh
An Arab merchant praises the cavalry and security of the Gurjara kingdom
Mahmud of Ghazni takes Kannauj after Rajyapala abandons it
Last inscription of the dynasty, issued by Yashahpala
Sanjaya erects a lingga on the hill at Canggal; the inscription names him Rakai Mataram Sang Ratu Sanjaya, lord of Mataram.
Panangkaran builds the Kalasan temple to the goddess Tara and a monastery for Buddhist monks of the Shailendra realm.
Javanese fleets raid Champa a second time and burn the temple at Phan Rang, after demolishing Po Nagar at Nha Trang in 774.
Samaratungga completes Borobudur, the stone mandala begun under Dharanindra.
The Shivagrha inscription records Rakai Pikatan's victory over a rebel in a hill fortress and the consecration of the Shiva temple at Prambanan.
On 10 May Balitung takes the throne, reunites the kingdom after thirteen years of turmoil and for the first time brings parts of East Java under Mataram.
Mpu Sindok moves the capital to Tamwlang in East Java and founds the Isyana dynasty.
Amoghavarsha I begins a 64-year reign and later founds Manyakheta
Krishna III defeats the Cholas at the Battle of Takkolam
The Paramara king Siyaka II sacks Manyakheta
Tailapa II overthrows Karka II and founds the Western Chalukya Empire
Jayavarman II is consecrated universal monarch on Phnom Kulen, founding the empire
Jayavarman VII, having expelled the Cham, subjugates Champa itself
Chinese envoy Zhou Daguan arrives and later writes a vivid account of Angkor
The Thai kingdom of Ayutthaya captures Angkor, by traditional dating
Traditional date for the fortification of Pagan
Anawrahta conquers the Mon city of Thaton, according to tradition
The four-language Myazedi inscription is set up
Mongol forces from Yunnan defeat Pagan at Ngasaunggyan
King Narathihapate is murdered as Yuan forces invade
The Myinsaing brothers depose Kyawswa, ending the dynasty
Tailapa II overthrows the Rashtrakuta king Karka II
The Chola king Rajadhiraja I is killed at the Battle of Koppam
Vikramaditya VI takes the throne and begins the Chalukya-Vikrama era
The Kalachuri Bijjala II takes royal titles at Kalyani
Vishnuvardhana’s forces take Talakad from the Cholas
The Chennakeshava temple at Belur is consecrated
Veera Ballala II assumes full imperial titles
The Keshava temple at Somanathapura is built
Malik Kafur captures the Hoysala capital Dwarasamudra
Veera Ballala III is killed fighting the Madurai Sultanate
Ulugh Khan annexes Madurai to the Delhi Sultanate
Sukaphaa crosses the Patkai hills into the upper Brahmaputra valley
Treaty of Asurar Ali fixes a frontier with the Mughal Empire
Mir Jumla's Mughal army occupies the Ahom capital Garhgaon
Lachit Borphukan defeats the Mughals at the Battle of Saraighat
Treaty of Yandabo: Burma renounces Assam, which passes to the East India Company
Date of the Ram Khamhaeng inscription; embassies to the Yuan court begin about this time
Li Thai takes the throne and begins a Buddhist revival
Ayutthaya is founded in the lower Chao Phraya basin
Sukhothai submits as a vassal of Ayutthaya
Sukhothai is absorbed into Ayutthaya on the death of Maha Thammaracha IV
Mangrai conquers the Mon kingdom of Hariphunchai
Mangrai founds Chiang Mai as his capital
The monk Sumana founds a new Buddhist lineage at Wat Suan Dok
Tilokarat convenes a Buddhist council at Wat Chet Yot
Bayinnaung of Burma captures Chiang Mai
A revolt in Chiang Mai expels the Burmese governor
Thonburi forces and northern lords take Chiang Mai from the Burmese
Jayakatwang of Kediri kills Kertanegara, ending the Singhasari kingdom
Raden Wijaya expels the Mongols and becomes Majapahit's first king
Forces directed by Gajah Mada subjugate Bali
Hayam Wuruk begins the reign that marks Majapahit's height
The Sundanese royal party is massacred at the Battle of Bubat
Mpu Prapanca completes the Nagarakretagama, describing the realm at its peak
The Madurai Sultanate is destroyed by Vijayanagara armies
Persian envoy Abdur Razzaq visits the capital
Krishnadevaraya defeats Bijapur at the Battle of Raichur
The Deccan sultanates defeat Vijayanagara at Talikota and sack the capital
Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah is proclaimed sultan at Daulatabad
The Jama Masjid in Gulbarga fort is built
Firuz Shah is defeated by Vijayanagara at Pangal
Mahmud Gawan's forces take Goa and his madrasa at Bidar is built
Mahmud Gawan is executed on a forged charge of treason
U Thong founds Ayutthaya and reigns as Ramathibodi I
Ayutthaya absorbs the kingdom of Sukhothai
Bayinnaung of Burma takes Ayutthaya after a long siege
Naresuan defeats the Burmese at the Battle of Nong Sarai
The Siamese envoy Kosa Pan is received by Louis XIV at Versailles
Phetracha seizes power and expels the French garrison
Konbaung armies sack and burn Ayutthaya
Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah unites Bengal as an independent sultanate
A Bengali embassy presents a giraffe to the Yongle Emperor
Alauddin Husain Shah becomes sultan, ending the Habshi period
Daud Khan Karrani is defeated at Rajmahal and Bengal passes to the Mughals
Fa Ngum is crowned king of Lan Xang
A Vietnamese army sent by Lê Thánh Tông sacks the capital
Setthathirath moves the capital to Vientiane
The great stupa of That Luang is built in Vientiane
Lan Xang becomes a vassal of Burma
The Dutch merchant Gerrit van Wuysthoff visits Vientiane
Lan Xang divides into the kingdoms of Luang Phrabang and Vientiane
A king of Po-ni visits the Ming court at Nanjing and dies there
Antonio Pigafetta describes the water city of Brunei
Spain captures the capital in the Castilian War but soon withdraws
Sarawak is granted to James Brooke
Brunei becomes fully independent under Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah
Yaduraya founds the Wodeyar dynasty, according to tradition
Raja Wodeyar I takes Srirangapatna and makes it his capital
Hyder Ali takes control of the government
Hyder Ali destroys a British detachment at the Battle of Pollilur
The Treaty of Mangalore ends the Second Anglo-Mysore War
Tipu Sultan cedes half his territory in the Treaty of Seringapatam
British forces storm Srirangapatna and Tipu Sultan is killed
The Yongle Emperor sends Yin Qing to Malacca; Zheng He follows in 1407 and takes Parameswara to China, recognising him as its ruler.
Ayutthaya invades by land and is beaten with the help of Tun Perak, who becomes Bendahara; a Siamese naval attack is repelled at Batu Pahat in 1456.
On 1 August Diogo Lopes de Sequeira arrives from Portugal; a plot to kill him fails, but several of his men are taken captive.
On 15 August Afonso de Albuquerque captures Malacca after a failed assault on 25 July; Mahmud Shah flees south.
The Portuguese raze Mahmud Shah's base at Bintan; he dies at Kampar two years later, and his sons found the Sultanates of Perak and Johor.
Paduka Batara and two other Sulu rulers visit the Ming court; he dies on the journey home
Spanish forces under Hurtado de Corcuera capture Jolo
Tausug warriors destroy the British post on Balambangan Island
Spanish steam gunboats destroy the Balangingi raiding bases
Sultan Jamalul Alam grants North Borneo to Overbeck and Dent
Jamalul Kiram II gives up temporal power under the Carpenter Agreement
Lê Lợi launches his revolt against Ming rule at Lam Sơn
Lê Lợi takes the throne as Lê Thái Tổ at Thăng Long
Lê Thánh Tông captures Vijaya, the capital of Champa
Mạc Đăng Dung seizes the throne and founds the Mạc dynasty
Lê and Trịnh forces retake Thăng Long from the Mạc
War between the Trịnh and Nguyễn lords begins; a truce follows in 1672
The Tây Sơn overthrow the Trịnh lords
Quang Trung defeats the Qing at Đống Đa; Lê Chiêu Thống flees to China
The Portuguese capture Goa from Bijapur
Bijapur and its allies defeat Vijayanagara at the Battle of Talikota
Ibrahim Adil Shah II annexes the Bidar Sultanate
Treaty with Shah Jahan makes Bijapur a Mughal tributary
Shivaji kills the Bijapur general Afzal Khan at Pratapgad
Aurangzeb takes Bijapur after a siege of more than a year
Ali Mughayat Syah conquers Pasai and drives out the Portuguese
Alauddin al-Kahhar besieges Malacca after seeking Ottoman military aid
Iskandar Muda sacks Batu Sawar, the capital of Johor
Aceh's armada is destroyed at Malacca by the Portuguese and their allies
Taj ul-Alam Safiatuddin becomes the first of four ruling queens
The Netherlands declares war, beginning the Aceh War
A Dutch expedition captures the sultan's palace
Sultan Muhammad Daud Syah surrenders to the Dutch
Guru Ram Das founds the city of Amritsar around its sacred pool
Guru Arjan installs the Adi Granth, the Sikh scripture, in the Harmandir Sahib at Amritsar
Guru Arjan is executed under the Mughal emperor Jahangir
Guru Tegh Bahadur is executed in Delhi on the orders of Aurangzeb
Guru Gobind Singh founds the Khalsa at Anandpur on the festival of Vaisakhi
Ranjit Singh takes Lahore and goes on to found the Sikh Empire
The Indian army’s Operation Blue Star at the Golden Temple, followed by the assassination of Indira Gandhi and anti-Sikh violence
Aceh sacks Johor's capital Batu Sawar
Johor and the Dutch take Malacca from the Portuguese
Sultan Mahmud Shah II is murdered, ending the Malacca line
Raffles recognises Hussein as sultan and founds British Singapore
The Anglo-Dutch Treaty splits the realm; Riau-Lingga goes to the Dutch sphere
Britain recognises Abu Bakar as Sultan of Johor
Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar becomes King of Malaysia
Surabaya surrenders to Sultan Agung after a long siege
First of two failed Mataram sieges of Dutch Batavia
Sultan Agung introduces the Javanese calendar
Trunajaya’s rebels sack the capital Plered
Rebels sack Kartasura during the Chinese War
The Treaty of Giyanti divides Mataram into Surakarta and Yogyakarta
Pegu falls and the First Toungoo Empire disintegrates
Anaukpetlun captures Syriam and executes Filipe de Brito
Chiang Mai is retaken and Lan Na returns to Burmese overlordship
Thalun moves the capital from Pegu to Ava
Thalun orders a kingdom-wide revenue inquest
The Burmese court hands the Ming Yongli Emperor to a Qing army
The Mon rise at Pegu and found the Restored Hanthawaddy Kingdom
Hanthawaddy forces capture Ava, ending the dynasty
Shivaji captures the fort of Torna, beginning his rise
Shivaji kills the Bijapur general Afzal Khan at Pratapgad
Shivaji is crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad, formally asserting sovereignty
Shivaji's son Sambhaji is executed during the long war with Aurangzeb
Peshwa Baji Rao I defeats the Nizam at Palkhed
Maratha armies reach Attock on the Indus
The Durrani army of Ahmad Shah Abdali crushes the Marathas at the Third Battle of Panipat
Peshwa Baji Rao II surrenders to the British and the Peshwa's office is abolished
Nizam-ul-Mulk defeats Mubariz Khan at Shakar Kheda
Baji Rao I defeats Nizam-ul-Mulk at Palkhed
Nizam Ali Khan moves the capital to Hyderabad
Subsidiary alliance with the East India Company
Berar’s revenues assigned to the British; Salar Jung I becomes chief minister
Mir Osman Ali Khan founds Osmania University
The Indian army takes over the state in Operation Polo
Hyderabad State is divided on linguistic lines
Marthanda Varma becomes king of Venad and begins to unify the small kingdoms of the south by brutal methods.
Travancore defeats the Dutch East India Company at the Battle of Colachel and captures Eustachius De Lannoy, who later modernises its army.
On 3 January Marthanda Varma dedicates Travancore to Padmanabha; the kings rule thereafter as servants of the deity.
Travancore defeats the Zamorin of Kozhikode at the battle of Purakkad and becomes the dominant state of Kerala.
On 28 December Tipu Sultan of Mysore attacks the Nedunkotta lines from the north and is defeated at the Battle of Nedumkotta.
Velu Thampi Dalawa's war on the East India Company is crushed; he kills himself to avoid capture and Travancore's forces are disbanded.
On 12 November Chithira Thirunal's Temple Entry Proclamation opens the temples of Travancore to the backward communities.
On 1 July Travancore, which acceded to the Indian Union on 12 August 1947, merges with Cochin to form the state of Travancore–Cochin.
Alaungpaya proclaims himself king at Moksobo (Shwebo)
Alaungpaya captures Pegu and reunites Burma
The last of four Qing invasions ends in the peace of Kaungton
Treaty of Yandabo ends the First Anglo-Burmese War
British forces take Mandalay; King Thibaw is exiled
Gorkhali troops capture Kathmandu during the Indra Jatra festival
A Qing army forces Nepal to make peace
Treaty of Sugauli ends the Anglo-Nepalese War
The Kot massacre brings Jang Bahadur Rana to power
Jang Bahadur issues the Muluki Ain law code
King Mahendra dismisses parliament and introduces the panchayat system
The Constituent Assembly abolishes the monarchy
Rama I founds the Chakri dynasty and moves the capital to Bangkok
Siamese forces crush Anouvong’s rebellion and sack Vientiane
The Bowring Treaty with Britain opens Siam to Western trade
French gunboats force the Chao Phraya; Siam cedes the lands east of the Mekong
The Slave Abolition Act completes the end of slavery
Siam joins the First World War on the Allied side
The People’s Party’s bloodless revolution ends absolute monarchy
Ranjit Singh, aged eighteen, seizes Lahore from its Bhangi chiefs
Ranjit Singh is proclaimed Maharaja of the Punjab on Baisakhi
The Treaty of Amritsar fixes the Sutlej as the Sikh-British boundary
The Sikhs occupy Peshawar, extending the empire to the Khyber Pass
Ranjit Singh dies, leaving the Lahore court to rival factions
Defeat at Sobraon ends the First Anglo-Sikh War; Kashmir is lost
Lord Dalhousie annexes the Punjab after the Second Anglo-Sikh War
The Dutch state takes over the possessions of the dissolved VOC
Johannes van den Bosch introduces the Cultivation System
The Dutch invade Aceh, beginning a decades-long war
Queen Wilhelmina announces the Ethical Policy
Japan conquers the colony; the Dutch surrender on 8 March
The Netherlands transfers sovereignty to Indonesia on 27 December
Nguyen Anh proclaims himself Gia Long and unites Vietnam
The Gia Long Code, modelled on Qing law, is issued
Minh Mang renames the country Dai Nam
A Franco-Spanish expedition attacks Da Nang
The Treaty of Saigon cedes three provinces of Cochinchina to France
Emperor Ham Nghi flees Hue and the Can Vuong resistance begins
Bao Dai abdicates to the Viet Minh on 30 August
The Government of India Act transfers the East India Company’s territories to the Crown
Queen Victoria is proclaimed Empress of India at the Delhi Durbar
The Indian National Congress is founded in Bombay
George V announces the move of the capital from Calcutta to Delhi
Troops kill hundreds of unarmed people at the Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar
Gandhi leads the Salt March to Dandi
Congress launches the Quit India movement
Independence and partition create India and Pakistan on 14–15 August
The Indian National Congress holds its first session in Bombay
Lord Curzon’s partition of Bengal provokes the Swadeshi movement and the boycott of British goods
Troops fire on an unarmed crowd at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar, killing hundreds
Gandhi’s Salt March to Dandi begins a nationwide campaign of civil disobedience
The Muslim League’s Lahore Resolution demands independent states for the Muslim-majority areas
The Congress launches the Quit India Movement, and its leaders are imprisoned
British rule ends, and British India is partitioned into India and Pakistan
France creates the Indochinese Union on 17 October
The Franco-Siamese crisis adds the Lao lands east of the Mekong
The seat of government moves from Saigon to Hanoi
The Indochinese Communist Party is founded and the Yen Bai mutiny is crushed
Japanese troops enter northern Indochina after France’s defeat
Japan overthrows French rule; Ho Chi Minh proclaims the Democratic Republic of Vietnam
The First Indochina War begins after fighting in Haiphong and Hanoi
Defeat at Dien Bien Phu and the Geneva Accords end French Indochina
Ugyen Wangchuck is unanimously chosen hereditary king of Bhutan by the Lhengye Tshog of leading monks, officials and heads of families.
The Treaty of Punakha gives Britain control of Bhutan's foreign affairs, making the kingdom in effect a British protectorate.
A treaty signed with newly independent India on 8 August continues the arrangement, India guiding Bhutan's external relations.
King Jigme Dorji Wangchuck establishes a 130-member National Assembly, followed by a Royal Advisory Council (1965) and a Cabinet (1968).
Bhutan is admitted to the United Nations after three years as an observer and is the first country to recognise Bangladesh's independence.
The first parliamentary elections are held, the Constitution establishes a parliamentary government, and Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck is crowned on 6 November.
The revised Indo-Bhutan Friendship Treaty comes into effect on 1 January, giving Bhutan full control of its foreign relations.
Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta proclaim independence on 17 August
The Netherlands transfers sovereignty after the Round Table Conference at The Hague
Indonesia hosts the Asian–African Conference at Bandung
A failed coup is followed by the mass killing of alleged communists
Suharto resigns during the Asian financial crisis
First direct presidential election; the Indian Ocean tsunami devastates Aceh
The Helsinki agreement ends the conflict in Aceh
Aung San and minority leaders agree to form a union at the Panglong Conference
The Union of Burma becomes independent on 4 January
General Ne Win seizes power and launches the Burmese Way to Socialism
A nationwide uprising is crushed and a new military junta takes power
The NLD of Aung San Suu Kyi wins an election the junta refuses to honour
Cyclone Nargis kills about 138,000 people in the Irrawaddy delta
Army operations drive over 700,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh
The military seizes power on 1 February, sparking nationwide armed resistance
Nine south-eastern states and two chiefships form a union with its capital at Kota (25 March)
Udaipur joins and Nehru inaugurates the United State of Rajasthan (18 April)
Jaipur, Jodhpur, Bikaner and Jaisalmer join to form Greater Rajasthan (30 March)
The Matsya Union of Alwar, Bharatpur, Dholpur and Karauli joins (15 May)
Sirohi joins and the union becomes the state of Rajasthan (26 January)
Ajmer and Mount Abu are added and the office of Rajpramukh abolished
The constitution comes into force and India becomes a republic on 26 January
China defeats India in the Sino-Indian War
India's victory in the Bangladesh Liberation War creates Bangladesh
Indira Gandhi declares the Emergency, suspending civil liberties until 1977
Operation Blue Star; Indira Gandhi assassinated; the Bhopal gas disaster
Economic liberalisation begins after a balance-of-payments crisis
Nuclear tests at Pokhran; India declares itself a nuclear-weapon state
Chandrayaan-3 lands near the Moon's south pole; India hosts the G20 summit
Pakistan adopts a republican constitution and becomes an Islamic republic with two geographically separate provinces, East Pakistan and West Pakistan.
President Iskander Mirza imposes martial law and is succeeded by General Ayub Khan, who suspends the constitution; a presidential constitution follows in 1962.
After the military refuses to transfer power to the Awami League and launches Operation Searchlight, war with India ends in defeat and East Pakistan becomes Bangladesh.
A military coup against Zulfikar Ali Bhutto's Pakistan Peoples Party ends democracy; General Zia-ul-Haq becomes president in 1978 and Islamises law and the economy.
Nawaz Sharif authorises nuclear tests in answer to India's, making Pakistan the seventh nuclear-armed state.
The Kargil War brings Pakistan and India to the brink, and General Pervez Musharraf takes power in a bloodless coup.
After Benazir Bhutto's assassination in 2007 the Pakistan Peoples Party wins the election; Musharraf resigns on 18 August and Asif Ali Zardari succeeds him.
The Pakistan Muslim League (N) wins the general election and Nawaz Sharif becomes prime minister for the third time, in the first successful democratic transition.
India and Yugoslavia first use the term non-alignment at the United Nations, refusing to take sides in the Korean War
The Bandung Conference of Asian and African states adopts a declaration that includes the Five Principles and a pledge of neutrality in the Cold War
Tito, Nehru and Nasser sign the Declaration of Brijuni in Yugoslavia
The first Conference of Heads of State or Government of Non-Aligned Countries meets in Belgrade
Fidel Castro chairs the Havana summit; months later the movement is split by the Soviet intervention in Afghanistan
The seventh summit, in New Delhi, calls the movement “history’s biggest peace movement”
The movement suspends the membership of Yugoslavia, a founding member, as the country breaks up
The 19th summit meets in Kampala, Uganda
Malaysia is proclaimed on 16 September; Indonesia steps up its Confrontation
Singapore is separated from the federation on 9 August
Racial riots of 13 May lead to emergency rule and the New Economic Policy
Mahathir Mohamad becomes prime minister, serving until 2003
Capital controls and the dismissal of Anwar Ibrahim spark the Reformasi movement
The Barisan Nasional loses power for the first time since independence
Anwar Ibrahim becomes prime minister of a unity government
Expelled from Malaysia, Singapore becomes an independent republic on 9 August, with Lee Kuan Yew as prime minister and Yusof bin Ishak as president.
Singapore co-founds the Association of Southeast Asian Nations and begins interchanging its dollar at par with Brunei's.
Britain withdraws its forces in October, leaving a token British, Australian and New Zealand presence; the Singapore Armed Forces, built with Israeli instructors, must guarantee independence.
Changi Airport opens, replacing Paya Lebar, as the Port of Singapore grows into one of the world's busiest and the economy turns to high-technology industry.
Goh Chok Tong succeeds Lee Kuan Yew as prime minister after 31 years; Nominated Members of Parliament are introduced the same year.
Lee Hsien Loong, Lee Kuan Yew's eldest son, becomes the third prime minister.
Lee Kuan Yew dies on 23 March and the nation mourns for a week; in September the PAP wins 69.9 percent of the vote.
Lawrence Wong becomes the fourth prime minister on 15 May, the first born after independence; his party wins 65.5 percent and 87 of 97 seats in 2025.
The Socialist Republic of Vietnam is proclaimed and Saigon renamed Ho Chi Minh City
Vietnam invades Cambodia and overthrows the Khmer Rouge in January 1979
China attacks across the northern border in the Sino-Vietnamese War
The Sixth Party Congress adopts the Doi Moi market reforms
The last Vietnamese troops withdraw from Cambodia
Vietnam normalises relations with the United States and joins ASEAN
Vietnam joins the World Trade Organization
Ties with the United States are raised to a comprehensive strategic partnership
On 28 November Fretilin unilaterally declares independence; nine days later, on 7 December, the Indonesian military invades East Timor.
The Indonesian military massacres more than 200 demonstrators, a turning point that brings international pressure on Indonesia.
A UN-supervised referendum votes clearly for independence; pro-integration militias backed by the Indonesian military answer with a campaign of violence, and INTERFET lands to restore order.
On 20 May the Constitution comes into force and Timor-Leste is recognised as independent by the UN, with Xanana Gusmão as its first president; it joins the UN on 27 September.
The Timor-Leste Petroleum Fund is established to turn oil and gas revenue into lasting wealth.
A crisis of unrest and factional fighting drives 155,000 people from their homes; UN security forces return to restore order.
Timor-Leste and Australia settle their maritime boundary by treaty after conciliation before the Permanent Court of Arbitration.
ASEAN announces that Timor-Leste will be admitted as its 11th full member at the October summit in Kuala Lumpur.
